titleStmt.title: A conceptual and methodological critique of internet addiction research: Towards a model of compensatory internet use
titleStmt.author: Daniel Kardefelt-Winther

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: A conceptual and methodological critique of internet addiction research: Towards a model of compensatory internet use

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: internet addiction research itself - its conceptual foundations and its reliance on direct-effects models
span.quote: This paper argues that conceptual issues and methodological shortcomings surrounding internet addiction research have made theoretical development difﬁcult.

span.label: why a field with so much collected data has produced so little theory, and whether compensation rather than compulsion better explains excessive internet use
span.quote: Despite much empirical data being collected and analyzed clear results and conclu- sions are surprisingly absent.

span.label: proposes the compensatory internet use model - the internet is used to alleviate a negative life situation - and argues the field must move from direct effects to mediation and interaction between psychosocial well-being and motivations
span.quote: An alternative model termed compensatory internet use is presented in an attempt to properly theorize the frequent assumption that people go online to escape real life issues or alleviate dysphoric moods and that this sometimes leads to negative outcomes.

span.label: critique
span.quote: In this paper I will develop the claim that internet addiction can be usefully approached from a perspective of compensation rather than compulsion.

span.label: people continuing to spend heavy time online despite experiencing outcomes that harm them
span.quote: This could help explain why some peo- ple keep spending so much time online despite experiencing negative outcomes.

span.label: conceptual and methodological critique of a research literature, followed by the construction of an alternative theoretical model and a proposed operationalisation
span.term: conceptual and methodological critique of a research literature, followed by the construction of an alternative theoretical model and a proposed operationalisation
span.quote: This paper will conclude by summarizing the elements of the compensatory internet use theory and suggest some implications for interpretation of results, empirical work and further theory building.

span.label: a lack in real life produces a motivation to go online, an application affords the missing thing, and the same act yields both the relief and the damage
span.quote: As an example, if real life is character- ized by a lack of social stimulation the individual reacts with a motivation to go online to socialize which is facilitated by an appli- cation where socializing is afforded, such as an online game or a so- cial networking site.

span.label: motivations MEDIATE between psychosocial well-being and excessive use - which is why a direct-effects design cannot see the process
span.quote: The theoretical argument is that by understanding how motivations mediate the relationship between psychosocial well-being and internet addiction, we can draw conclusions about how online activities may compensate for psychosocial problems.

span.label: the harm scales with how much compensation the person needs, so a permanent real-life difficulty implies a permanent demand
span.quote: For individuals with permanent real life issues, such as physical handicaps or dis- abilities, the need for compensation may be constant as case study evidence provided by Grifﬁths (2000) would suggest.

span.label: the model's testable prediction: escapism should predict problematic outcomes MORE strongly in high-stress people than low-stress ones
span.quote: According to a model of compensatory internet use, the relationship between escapism and problematic outcomes should be stronger for people with higher levels of stress, compared to those with lower levels of stress.

span.label: the compensatory model is proposed and argued here, not tested - the paper asks for the empirical work rather than reporting it
span.quote: The model of compensatory internet use suggests that researchers need to empirically investigate the relationship between motiva- tions and psychosocial well-being in the context of excessive internet use.

span.label: the paper leaves open whether the phenomenon should be called addiction at all
span.quote: Whether this is what we wish to call internet addiction or not can be debated, as can the compulsive nature of such inter- net use, but to suggest that this is a mental disorder seems to be a stretch. 3.

span.label: the field it critiques cannot isolate causes because nearly everything tested came out significant
span.quote: However, because most factors were found to be signiﬁcant predic- tors it has not been possible to make any claims about unique risk factors which has made it difﬁcult to isolate the causes behind internet addiction.

span.label: the compensation idea is old and repeatedly stated; what is missing is that almost nobody has tested it
span.quote: However, while plenty of speculation has surrounded the idea of compensatory internet use few studies have empirically investi- gated the compensatory potential of internet applications in the context of excessive internet use.

span.label: Kubey and Csikszentmihalyi's finding that people watch heavy TV in dysphoric states, carried across to the internet as self-medication
span.quote: Similar ideas about the compen- satory potential of media use was suggested in an early study by Kubey and Csikszentmihalyi (1990), who claimed that people were more likely to engage in bouts of heavy TV watching when they were in dysphoric states.

span.label: the historical move from direct effects to mediating variables is proposed as the transition internet addiction research must now make
span.quote: Williams, Yee, & Caplan (2008) have argued that game re- search needs to undergo the same transition as early communi- cation research did, where the direct effects model was made more nuanced by the addition of mediating variables.

span.label: Ingleby's argument that the governing principles of a field are philosophical rather than empirical, applied to why more findings have not produced theory
span.quote: What matters, Ingleby argues, are the fundamental principles which gov- ern the acquisition and interpretation of ‘‘ﬁndings’’; and these principles, although they are governed by matters of fact, are not themselves discovered empirically – they are as much philosophi- cal as scientiﬁc ones (p. 24).

span.label: controlling for stress when testing loneliness and social anxiety against excessive online gaming
span.note: eliminates: the possibility that loneliness and social anxiety are independent predictors rather than artefacts of being tested alone · outcome: failed
span.quote: Furthermore, as I discussed in a recent article (Kardefelt-Winther, 2014) the associations for both loneliness and social anxiety with excessive online gaming lost signiﬁcance when stress was controlled for.

span.label: controlling for psychosocial well-being when relating gaming motivations to internet addiction
span.note: eliminates: the possibility that the motivation-addiction association is spurious · outcome: held
span.quote: Importantly, in the study by Caplan et al. (2009) psychosocial well-being was controlled for as they suspected that associations between psycho- social well-being or motivations for play and internet addiction may be spurious.

span.label: internet addiction
span.quote: Most research on internet addiction is based on initial research by Young (1998), who conceptualized internet addiction as an impulse-control disorder, deriving diagnostic criteria from the Diagnostic and Statis- tical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-IV) diagnosis for pathological gambling.

span.label: compensatory internet use
span.quote: The basic tenet of the theory of compensatory internet use is that the locus of the problem is a reaction by the individual to his negative life situation, facilitated by an internet application.

span.label: direct effects
span.quote: Traditionally, research on internet addiction has focused on direct effects models exploring the associations between psychological vulnerabilities and internet addiction.

span.label: motivations
span.quote: There seems to be an opportunity here to combine the psychological approach with the motivations approach through the model of compensa- tory internet use.

span.label: psychosocial well-being
span.quote: In terms of research operationalization, this can be tested by exploring whether the association between moti- vations and internet addiction vary depending on the level of psy- chosocial well-being.

span.label: escapism
span.quote: Kardefelt-Winther (2014) demonstrated empirically that the moti- vations escapism and achievement mediated the relationship between stress and excessive online gaming.

span.label: coping strategy
span.quote: I argue that it can be better understood as a coping strategy grounded in under- standable (but not always healthy) motivations.

span.label: affordances
span.quote: These recent discussions take the idea of com- pensatory internet use to a more detailed level where applications are assumed to have different compensatory potential depending on their affordances.

span.label: interaction effects
span.quote: Because the model does not assume a direct relationship between psycho- social well-being and internet addiction, interaction effects be- tween the elements in the model constitute the analytical focus.

span.label: internet addiction - the pathological sense, an impulse-control disorder with criteria borrowed from pathological gambling
span.quote: who conceptualized internet addiction as an impulse-control disorder, deriving diagnostic criteria from the Diagnostic and Statis- tical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-IV) diagnosis for pathological gambling.

span.label: internet addiction - the compensatory sense, a practical response to an unmet need that sometimes costs more than it returns
span.quote: It is an understandable and practical way to acquire social stimulation when there is a lack of it (e.g., Chappell, Eatough, Davies & Grifﬁths, 352 D.

span.label: internet addiction - the normative-shift reading, where the symptom is a new way of living that only has pathological interpretations available
span.quote: have suggested that what is treated by researchers as pathological behaviour may be a new way of life for which researchers currently have only path- ological interpretations.

span.label: `internet addiction` - THREE COMPETING LABELS FOR THE SAME THING, DECLARED IN THE PAPER'S FIRST FOOTNOTE: `EXCESSIVE INTERNET USE, COMPULSIVE INTERNET USE, PROBLEMATIC INTERNET USE - labels that have been USED INTERCHANGEABLY TO DESCRIBE MORE OR LESS THE SAME CONCEPT`. And `more or less` is doing work: the paper's whole argument is that the concept is not stable.
span.quote: Or excessive internet use, compulsive internet use, problematic internet use – labels that have been used interchangeably to describe more or less the same concept

span.label: critiques → Young (1998), who built internet addiction on the DSM-IV criteria for pathological gambling
span.quote: Since addictions were not acknowledged in DSM-IV, Young contended that the diagnosis of pathological gambling was most akin to the pathological nature of internet use and adopting the criteria would be helpful in clinical settings and stimulate further research (Young, 1998).

span.label: contradicts → the direct-effects tradition in internet addiction research
span.quote: A direct effects approach has not allowed researchers to explore the signiﬁcant predictors of internet addiction while controlling for interactions with other inﬂuencing psychosocial conditions or mediating variables.

span.label: builds-on → Ingleby (1981) on epistemological issues in psychiatry
span.quote: What is needed, then, is not more ﬁnd- ings but a reappraisal of the kind of explanations we should be looking for.

span.label: builds-on → Wood (2008), that addiction concerns the interaction between individual, culture and environment
span.quote: This follows on Wood’s (2008) observation that theories of addiction are increas- ingly moving away from a focus on the activity or substance as a causal factor and instead suggesting that ‘‘addiction concerns the interaction between the individual, their culture and their environ- ment’’ (p. 177).

span.label: builds-on → Kardefelt-Winther (2014), the author's own finding that escapism and achievement mediate stress and excessive gaming
span.quote: Indeed, following on Caplan et al.’s (2009) study, Kardefelt-Winther (2014) demonstrated empirically that the moti- vations escapism and achievement mediated the relationship between stress and excessive online gaming.

span.label: critiques → Young's edited volume (2011), offered as evidence that the field has explanations but no consensus
span.quote: The lack of theoretical development is evident in Young’s edited book (2011) where each chapter suggests different causes for internet addiction.

span.label: compensatory internet use —distinct-from→ internet addiction
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.95 — the paper's central move
span.quote: In this paper I will develop the claim that internet addiction can be usefully approached from a perspective of compensation rather than compulsion.

span.label: direct effects —contrasted-with→ interaction effects
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.9
span.quote: Because the model does not assume a direct relationship between psycho- social well-being and internet addiction, interaction effects be- tween the elements in the model constitute the analytical focus.

span.label: loneliness and social anxiety stopped predicting excessive online gaming once stress was controlled for
span.quote: Furthermore, as I discussed in a recent article (Kardefelt-Winther, 2014) the associations for both loneliness and social anxiety with excessive online gaming lost signiﬁcance when stress was controlled for.

span.label: escapism and achievement mediated the relationship between stress and excessive online gaming
span.quote: Indeed, following on Caplan et al.’s (2009) study, Kardefelt-Winther (2014) demonstrated empirically that the moti- vations escapism and achievement mediated the relationship between stress and excessive online gaming.

span.label: nearly every psychosocial factor tested came out a significant predictor, which is why none could be isolated as a cause
span.quote: However, because most factors were found to be signiﬁcant predic- tors it has not been possible to make any claims about unique risk factors which has made it difﬁcult to isolate the causes behind internet addiction.

span.label: adding the activity and the motivation to the model lets a result state WHY someone is online rather than only that they are at risk
span.quote: Using this model researchers could describe the observed situation in greater detail: ‘‘a player of World of Warcraft (a) who wants to socialize (b) and chat (b) with other players, and is high on social anxiety (1), may be at increased risk of neglecting schoolwork (2) and of having conﬂicts with parents due to their engagement with the internet (2)’’.

span.label: internet addiction as a lost-control state with problematic outcomes
span.quote: This could help explain why some peo- ple keep spending so much time online despite experiencing negative outcomes.

span.label: the basic tenet of compensatory internet use - the locus of the problem is the reaction, not the application
span.quote: The basic tenet of the theory of compensatory internet use is that the locus of the problem is a reaction by the individual to his negative life situation, facilitated by an internet application.

span.label: the compensatory model stated as a proposal about negative life situations giving rise to a motivation
span.quote: This paper proposes a theory of compensatory internet use where negative life situations can give rise to a motivation to go online to alleviate negative feelings.

span.label: the four elements of the proposed model: psychosocial vulnerabilities, problematic outcomes, the online activity and its affordances, and motivations
span.quote: This paper suggests an inclusion of two additional elements that have been mentioned in this paper: the online activity and its affordances (a) and motivations for going online (b).

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chb.2013.10.059.
